messages.subject: How do I install custom fonts in shinyapps.io apps (for base graphics, not html content)?
messages.subject_clean: How do I install custom fonts in shinyapps.io apps (for base graphics, not html content)?
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to install a custom font eg Roboto <https://www.google.com/fonts#UsePlace:use/Collection:Roboto> to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> apps?

I want to make base graphics with (client) custom font labels, so the font needs to be on the system and registered with R to be accessible.

I already tried extrafont::ttf_import() and that failed because it looks for a local path in the extrafontsdb and returns an error like the below (slightly edited for confidentiality) log output from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

2015-10-01T16:27:55.642720+00:00 shinyapps[62561]: Scanning ttf files in /srv/connect/apps/my_test_app/www/fonts/ ...
2015-10-01T16:27:55.643122+00:00 shinyapps[62561]: Extracting .afm files from .ttf files...
2015-10-01T16:27:55.722440+00:00 shinyapps[62561]: /srv/connect/apps/my_test_app/www/fonts/my_custom_font/my_custom_font_bold-webfont.ttfWarning in gzfile(dest, "w") :
2015-10-01T16:27:55.722442+00:00 shinyapps[62561]:   cannot open compressed file '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/extrafontdb/metrics/my_custom_font_bold-webfont.afm.gz', probable reason 'Permission denied'
2015-10-01T16:27:55.722918+00:00 shinyapps[62561]: Error in gzfile(dest, "w") : cannot open the connection

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] How do I install custom fonts in shinyapps.io apps (for base graphics, not html content)?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] How do I install custom fonts in shinyapps.io apps (for base graphics, not html content)?
messages.body_plain:
Sure. Basically the steps look like this:

1. dir.create('~/.fonts')
2. Download the fonts, e.g. via download.file(), to ~/.fonts
3. Run system('fc-cache -f ~/.fonts')

You probably only want to do this when Sys.info()[['sysname']] ==
'Linux' since this does not make sense to Windows.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: Help obtaining file
messages.subject_clean: Help obtaining file
messages.body_plain:
Hi ShinyApps,

I was able to resolve an issue with building a model on a different endian-ness (my system is 64 bit, the shinyapps server is 32 bit) by building the app on the server whenever it starts running. However, this is of course slow and not ideal - I would like to deploy the model with the app so it doesn't need to be built. I don't have a 32 but system and my efforts have so far failed, as have my efforts to save as an RDA file, and then download the path. It also seems that when I download the app as a package it doesn't include any files produced at runtime. Could you give suggestions for how to best obtain the model that we build? Is it something that you would be able to retrieve for us? It is the "model.rda" file that is currently being saved in the app base directory, and the app is at:

https://predict.shinyapps.io/raps

Please note that it takes about a minute to build the model, and then show the result on the bottom.

Many thanks,

Vanessa

messages.body_plain:
Vanessa,
I am a little confused I must admit.  shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> isn't 32 bit.  If the question is that you have built a model on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> that you want to be able to download, I think there are two paths that you could follow.

1. You could provide a link in your UI that allows you to download the file over http.
2. You could have your application write out the model to a centralized storage location that is accessible outside of shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef

messages.subject_clean: Oracle Database Package Fails on Deployment
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm currently developing an Shiny App which connects to an Oracle Database in the company I work at.
The app is working like a charm locally, however when I try to deploy it through ShinyApp.io it starts by installing all the packages and when it gets to ROracle  <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ROracle/ROracle.pdf>package it returns the following error:
[2015-10-08T10:43:41.675492602+0000] Building R package: ROracle (1.2-1)
/mnt/packages/build /mnt
* installing to library ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library’
* installing *source* package ‘ROracle’ ...
** package ‘ROracle’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
configure: error: OCI libraries not found
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘ROracle’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/ROracle’
################################# End Task Log ################################# Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 88404593 failed: Error building image: Error building ROracle (1.2-1). Build exited with non-zero status: 1

I'm running the following code to Deploy:
shinyapps::deployApp('C://Users/oracle/Documents/repo/repositório/Produtos/Shiny')

Anyone had this problem before or used  ROracle in a Shiny App ?

Any other code snippets that would help solving it please ask and I'll post it.
Thanks in advance!

messages.body_plain:
Hello guys I am trying to get reportingTools to work with DeSeq and R Shiny. The whole idea is to write a shiny app using the code example given by reportingTools here for DeSeq  <http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ReportingTools/inst/doc/rnaseqAnalysis.pdf>. ReportingTools makes some suggestions code in order to work with shiny also here <http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ReportingTools/inst/doc/shiny.pdf> . with this knowledge i came out with my server.r and ui.r codes below:

ui.R

library(ReportingTools)
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  custHeaderPanel("ReportingTools",
                  js = list.files(system.file("extdata/jslib", package="ReportingTools"),
                                  full.names=TRUE),
                  css = list.files(system.file("extdata/csslib", package="ReportingTools"),
                                   pattern="bootstrap.css", full.names=TRUE),
  ),

  sidebarPanel(

  ),

  mainPanel(

    htmlOutput("view2")
  )
))

and

server.R

library(ReportingTools)
library(shiny)
library(DESeq)

##custom rendering function for server.R
renderRepTools = function(expr, env=parent.frame(), quoted=FALSE) {
  func <- exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
  function(){
    paste(capture.output(func()), collapse="\n")
  }
}

##open the report with the shinyHandlers
htmlrep = HTMLReport(reportDirectory = "./",shortName="bigtest", handlers = shinyHandlers)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  data(mockRnaSeqData)
  cds<-newCountDataSet(mockRnaSeqData, conditions)
  cds<-estimateSizeFactors(cds)
  cds<-estimateDispersions(cds)
  res<-nbinomTest(cds,"control", "case" )

  ###use RT to display output
  output$view2 <- renderRepTools({
    publish(res,htmlrep,name="df",countTable=mockRnaSeqData, pvalueCutoff=0.05,conditions=conditions,annotation.db="org.Mm.eg.db",
            expName="deseq",reportDir="./", .modifyDF=makeDESeqDF)
  })
})

This seems to slowly generate a reportingTool table after about 2 minutes of waiting after running the code however even though the images seems to be available in the report directory they fail to show up?

Anyone knows why this is so or yet still a better idea of how to get R shiny to display this code for DeSEq from the manual here <http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ReportingTools/inst/doc/rnaseqAnalysis.pdf> ?

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] issue with terms - sleeping, running, idle ...
messages.body_plain:
Hi Davide,
Thanks for the kind words.  An application on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> will be brought online when it gets its first request.  It will stay up and active until the last connection drops out, and the idle timeout is reached at which point it will put itself to sleep.    "Idle" means an application is up, but isn't being interacted with from any clients, there is a default timeout of 15 minutes built into the platform which will put the application to sleep, you can override that if you want and bring that down to 5 minutes. The active hours is literally the sum of minutes that the application was up for the month.

Hope this helps, and best of luck exploring the platform.

-Tareef

messages.body_plain:
Just to confirm Aaron, are you saying that for any given end user who is going through the survey they may take 10-15 minutes to fill it out? Or are you saying that there is a 10-15 minutes of computation per user?
If it is the former, I would guess that you might be able to get it done at the lower plans as long as the computational needs of the survey are modest.  If you need more horse power you will want to be at the $39 plan at a minimum.
The key thing to keep in mind is that as you add multiple instances or R workers you need to make sure that you are writing your survey results to a data store that handles concurrency well.

> StrictHostKeyChecking=no

when you create the ssh tunnel? Is this not a security risk?

Cheers

On Monday, March 30, 2015 at 10:46:21 AM UTC-4, Phill Clarke wrote:
> Hi Mike,
>
> I did get this to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, with help from Tareef and Chad. They were going to write up the process. However, in short:
>
> 1. Create a set of SSH keys on your local machine
>
> 2. Add the relevant key to your database server. I used ssh-copy-id for this. There are many tutorials online. I use Digital Ocean and this is a good start: https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-configure-ssh-key-based-authentication-on-a-linux-server
>
> 3. Upload both public and private SSH key into a directory accessible from your Shiny app. I initially had some reservations about uploading the private key, but after thinking about it the alternative is an SSH tunnel initiated through username/password which is just as insecure, maybe more. Effectively your Shiny app server needs the private key because it's really taking the place of your local machine when making the SSH tunnel.
>
> 4. Then I have the following code (change credentials as appropriate):
>
> # Load db connector library
>
> library("RMySQL")
>
> # Change permissions on SSH keys
>
> system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa.pub"))
> system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa"))
>
> # Open SSH connection
>
> system(paste("ssh -v -f -N -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -i /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa -L 3306:localhost:3306 user@hostname sleep 20"))
>
> # Database query
>
> con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host='127.0.0.1', user='youDBUser', password='yourDBPassword', dbname='yourDBName')
>
> sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM database.tablename", sep="")
>
> queryResults <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
>
> dbDisconnect(con)
>
> Key things to remember here are the path to the SSH key, make sure the directory where the SSH keys are located is writable and your user has rights to change the permissions, make sure port 3306 is open on both machines.
>
> I think that's it. It took me a few attempts, with some rookie errors, but with Tareef and Chad's help we found success.
>
> Good luck.
>
> Cheers
> Phill
>

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shinyapps.io monitoring
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Shinyapps.io monitoring
messages.body_plain:
Avner,

You could use a monitoring system such as Pingdom <https://www.pingdom.com/>. However I would advise against it. The reason is that when applications running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> are not in use (e.g. have had 0 connections for 15 minutes), they go to sleep. While application are asleep, they do not use active hours. A web monitoring system such as Pingdom, will make periodic requests to the application to check if its up or not. This will have the effect of waking the application up and it consume hours even though no real person is using it.

-Andy

messages.subject_clean: Unable to deploy packages in Bioconductor using Shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
This is a bit odd. Normally, packages from BioConductor do not have a `Repository:` field set in their DESCRIPTION; however, they do come with a `biocViews` field in their DESCRIPTION.

Can you copy the contents of that package's DESCRIPTION file here? You can get it with something like:

    readLines(system.file("DESCRIPTION", package = "ComplexHeatmap"))

We might need to check for `biocViews` before checking / validating the repository.

Yes, unfortunately we don't have SQLServer drivers installed on the server so it isn't able to connect to your database.
We currently only support open source databases on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but we are watching to see if we get a lot more requests for proprietary databases.

Andy corrected me (while on vacation) and let me know that you can make this work by using the FreeTDS driver.  I am not an expert on this, but if you change your code to something like this:

odbcDriverConnect("driver=FreeTDS;Server=hostname;database=dbname;uid=username;pwd=password")

We don't have any DSNs configured, but you can see tips for how to do this here:

Hi Hanno,
I must admit I am a little confused about the use case you are describing.  Are you asking if it would be easy to make a shiny application that essentially allows multiple people to edit the content of the page? What is the content of the page?  Shiny is a framework that makes it easy to create interactive web applications out of your R analyses, and although you could create different types of web applications with it, it isn't really meant to replace more general purpose web frameworks which are likely to be better suited for non statistical analyses use cases.

Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] A wiki for shiny apps
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] A wiki for shiny apps
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks for the answer and sorry about the confusion. I am not really sure myself about technically how the idea would work.

The idea would be to make the app so that people can edit it like people can edit a wikipedia page.
I don't think the shiny app should replace the general purpose web framework - I'm hoping more that the shiny app would bring all the statistical analysis possibilities to everyone. At the moment (as much as I know) all the statistical programs are quite complex and often not for free. I think R itself is too complex for many applications. But with this kind of a wiki with simple shiny apps offering statistical tools to everyone openly it would make things a lot easier for people.

I'm a chemistry PhD student and I see that these apps could be very useful for e.g. chemists or life scientists who need to do statistical analysis of their data. But the programs are complex and the statistics they need to use is complex - the result is that the scientists spend a lot of time studying statistics and the programs (and therefore not working on the topic they should be focusing on) and then it is still quite possible that the statistics is used in a wrong way (e.g. you can find numerous articles on how scientists often misinterpret the results of statistical tests because they don't understand quite correctly what the p-value they obtain means). That's the problem I'm hoping to solve with this wiki. Shiny apps could be made simple to learn and use, and quite foolproof so that results are not misinterpreted. And of course they can be made free for everyone.

I hope I clarified my question a little bit now.

All the best,
Hanno

Shiny is a framework that makes it easy to create interactive web applications out of your R analyses, and although you could create different types of web applications with it, it isn't really meant to replace more general purpose web frameworks which are likely to be better suited for non statistical analyses use cases.

The reason is that when applications running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> are not in use (e.g. have had 0 connections for 15 minutes), they go to sleep. While application are asleep, they do not use active hours. A web monitoring system such as Pingdom, will make periodic requests to the application to check if its up or not. This will have the effect of waking the application up and it consume hours even though no real person is using it.

At the moment (as much as I know) all the statistical programs are quite complex and often not for free. I think R itself is too complex for many applications. But with this kind of a wiki with simple shiny apps offering statistical tools to everyone openly it would make things a lot easier for people.
>
> I'm a chemistry PhD student and I see that these apps could be very useful for e.g. chemists or life scientists who need to do statistical analysis of their data. But the programs are complex and the statistics they need to use is complex - the result is that the scientists spend a lot of time studying statistics and the programs (and therefore not working on the topic they should be focusing on) and then it is still quite possible that the statistics is used in a wrong way (e.g. you can find numerous articles on how scientists often misinterpret the results of statistical tests because they don't understand quite correctly what the p-value they obtain means). That's the problem I'm hoping to solve with this wiki. Shiny apps could be made simple to learn and use, and quite foolproof so that results are not misinterpreted. And of course they can be made free for everyone.
>
> I hope I clarified my question a little bit now.
>
> All the best,
> Hanno
>

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Unable to deploy app on shiny server: Getting following: Error building image: Error building RGtk2 (2.20.31). Build exited with non-zero status: 1.
messages.body_plain:
Are you sure you're not using it? Remember any files that exist in the same directory are considered part of the app, so you need to make sure library(rattle) or require(rattle) appears nowhere.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Problem when publishing: "Account" and "Application" are blank
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Problem when publishing: "Account" and "Application" are blank
messages.body_plain:
Hi Colby,

This error usually results from including Shiny content in your document, but not marking the document itself as Shiny. Can you try a few things?

1. Add "runtime: shiny" to your YAML header. For instance:

---
title: "My document"
author: "Me"
runtime: shiny
---

shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is designed to host Shiny content (you can use RPubs if you're just publishing non-interactive R Markdown docs).

2. Can you paste the relevant portion of the doc (around the line number associated with the error, if any)?

Jonathan.

>
> "Content not publishable"
>
> I get a warning in the console when I knit HTML
> "Shiny application in a static R Markdown document
> Error: path for html_dependency not provided"
>
> On Mon, Oct 26, 2015 at 2:47 PM, Andy Kipp <an...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > Have you tried updating to the latest version of RStudio?
> >
> > I think this issue is fixed in 0.99.

Fereshteh

Hi,

I've tried to deploy my Shiny app to the shiny.io <http://shiny.io> server, but it ends up greyed out as soon as it's deployed. I checked the shiny logs, and it shows an error:

"ERROR: there is no package called 'gplots'"

The first line of my server file is "library(gplots)". I have also tried "require(gplots)" but I still get the same error.

I'm running Windows 7, and the gplots package is installed locally under my own user folder -- so when I try to run the app locally I have no problems, but I can't deploy it successfully.

I've tried looking up help on this error but all the examples I could find were for Linux users.

Please tell me what I can do to get shiny.io <http://shiny.io> to install the package correctly.

Thanks,

Louise
